answer.policy_title: Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026
criteria_quotes: femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:

◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Arthroscopic or Open Hip Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI) Non-Indications CMM.JT.NI.314 v1.0.2026 Not Medically Necessary • Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition, including ANY of the following radiographic findings:

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Synovectomy Indications CMM.JT.IN.314 v1.0.2026 Synovectomy is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Synovectomy Non-Indications CMM.JT.NI.314 v1.0.2026 Not Medically Necessary • Synovectomy is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition.

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Procedures and Conditions Not Addressed Elsewhere Indications CMM.JT.IN.314 v1.0.2026 Arthroscopic or open hip surgery is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following:
• Based on lack of scientific evidence of efficacy and safety, "in-office" diagnostic arthroscopy (e.g., Mi-Eye™, VisionScope®) is considered not medically necessary.

Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven (EIU) • Capsular plication is considered experimental, investigational, or unproven • Anterior inferior iliac spine/subspinous decompression is considered experimental, investigational, or unproven.
answer.submission_route: Log in at my.cigna.com to find your plan's appeal form and submit it there, or call the number on your card. The mailing address is plan-specific — use the one on your denial letter. Online: my.cigna.com By phone: 1-800-244-6224, or the number on your card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
